{{ill|Asakuma Shrine|ja|朝熊神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asakuma Shrine|qq=}} is an {{ill|setsumatsusha|lt=auxiliary shrine (sessha)|ja|末社|lt=Sessha|1=Setsumatsusha|2=ja|3=摂末社|4=zh|5=攝末社|6=es|7=Setsumatsusha|8=fr|9=Setsumatsusha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/setsumatsusha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 摂末社}} of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|lt=Inner Shrine (Kōtai Jingū)|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} at {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}. It holds the highest Rank among the Inner Shrine's auxiliary shrines<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 108</ref>. This article also covers {{ill|Asakuma Shrine|ja|朝熊御前神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asakuma Gozen Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 朝熊神社 (伊勢市)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17191186}}, which shares the same grounds.
Asakuma Shrine is a highly prestigious shrine within the Inner Shrine network and hosts more {{ill|Festival|ja|祭祀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto rituals|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祭|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q132241}} than other auxiliary shrines<ref name="ic"/>.
== Overview ==
Located at 2566-1 Sakura-gi, Asakuma-cho, {{ill|Ise, Mie|en|Ise, Mie|qid=Q328067|lt=Ise, Mie}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}<ref name="sk88">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p. 188</ref>, the shrine sits on a hill east of the confluence of the {{ill|Isuzu River|en|Isuzu River|qid=Q6089522|lt=Isuzu River}} and Asakuma River<ref name="nk5">Tanigawa (1986): p. 45</ref>. Across the Asakuma River lies {{ill|Kagami-no-Miya Shrine (Naiku)|lt=Kagami-no-Miya Shrine (Naiku)|lt=Kagami-no-Miya|ja|鏡宮神社 (伊勢市)|1=Kagami-no-Miya Shrine (Naiku)|lt=Kagami-no-Miya Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagami-no-Miya|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagami-no-Miya Shrine (Naiku)|qq=}}<ref name="nk5"/>.
Both shrines have deep ties with the Isuzu River<ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p. 60</ref>. Upon entering the grounds, Asakuma Shrine is on the right (east), and Asakuma Gozen Shrine is on the left (west)<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>. The proper order of worship is to visit Asakuma Shrine first, followed by Asakuma Gozen Shrine<ref name="gk"/>. The shrine grounds cover approximately 5,002 m²<ref name="uy">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): p. 9</ref>.
Like many auxiliary shrines, no {{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/offertory box|qid=Q135491444}} is present. Both shrine buildings face southwest.
== Asakuma Shrine ==
Asakuma Shrine holds the top Rank among the Inner Shrine's auxiliary shrines and receives ceremonial treatment akin to the {{ill|betsugu|ja|別宮|lt=Betsugū|1=Setsumatsusha|2=ja|3=摂末社|4=zh|5=攝末社|6=es|7=Setsumatsusha|8=fr|9=Setsumatsusha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/betsugu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} shrines<ref name="ic"/>. Similarly, {{ill|Kusanagi Shrine (Ise)|ja|草奈伎神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusanagi Shrine (Ise)|qq=}}, the highest auxiliary shrine of {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyōke Daijingū|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Outer Shrine), enjoys special privileges<ref>Sakurai (1969): p. 91</ref>.
The name "Asakuma" (朝熊) is believed to derive from "Asakuma" (浅隈), meaning a "shallow meandering river"<ref name="gk"/>. Other theories suggest it refers to a bear appearing during {{ill|Kūkai|en|Kūkai|qid=Q222227|lt=Kūkai}}'s ascetic training or relates to {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|en|Konohanasakuya-hime|qid=Q1781862|lt=Konohanasakuya-hime}}'s alternative name "Ashizu-hime"<ref name="sk88"/>.
The shrine building follows the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545|lt=shinmei-zukuri}} architectural style, with a wooden shingle roof, surrounded by a single layer of {{ill|Sacred fences|en|Tamagaki|qid=Q3078312|lt=tamagaki}} (sacred fence)<ref name="sk93">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p. 193</ref>. There is one {{ill|Torii|ja|神明鳥居|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shinmei torii|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鳥居|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q234731}}<ref name="sk93"/>.
=== Enshrined Deities ===
The shrine enshrines {{ill|Toshigami|lt=Toshigami|lt=Ōtoshi-no-Kami|ja|大歳神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtoshi-no-Kami|qq=}}, Koke-mushi-no-Kami (苔虫神), and Asakuma Mizu-no-Kami (朝熊水神)<ref name="ic"/>. These three deities are considered the {{ill|guardian deities|ja|守護神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/guardian deities|qq=}} of the Asakuma plain, associated with {{ill|Five Grains|en|Five Grains|qid=Q1191138|lt=agriculture}} and {{ill|Suijin|en|Suijin|qid=Q3137449|lt=water god}}<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>.
== Asakuma Gozen Shrine ==
Ranked second among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine<ref>Ujiyamada City Office (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>, its structure is identical to Asakuma Shrine's<ref name="sk93"/>. The enshrined deity is Asakuma Gozen-no-Kami (朝熊御前神)<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>.
Initially, {{ill|Kagami-no-Miya Shrine (Naiku)|lt=Kagami-no-Miya Shrine (Naiku)|lt=Kagami-no-Miya|ja|鏡宮神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagami-no-Miya|qq=}} served as the front shrine (御前社) for Asakuma Shrine when it was rebuilt in 1663<ref name="nk1">Tanigawa (1986): p. 51</ref>. Later, Asakuma Gozen Shrine was constructed next to Asakuma Shrine, with Kagami-no-Miya becoming an independent shrine<ref name="nk1"/>.
== History ==
According to the {{ill|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato-hime-no-mikoto Seiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=}}, Princess {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} established Asakuma Shrine in the 27th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin}}'s reign to enshrine a stone manifestation of Ōtoshi-no-Kami<ref name="sk89"/>. Based on the definition of Ise Jingū's auxiliary shrines, it was founded before {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q97379316}} 5 (927)<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22</ref>.
Records indicate that during the {{ill|Northern and Southern Courts period (disambiguation)|en|Northern and Southern Courts period (disambiguation)|qid=Q8140349|lt=Nanboku-chō period}}, rice tributes (役夫工米) were levied for shrine construction<ref name="nk6"/>. Although reconstruction records ceased afterward, rituals continued until the {{ill|Sengoku Period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q117415390}}<ref>Tanigawa (1986): pp. 46–47</ref>.
Thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kiyonaga Kawabe|ja|河辺精長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q92924151}} (Ōnakatomi Masanaga), the shrine was restored in July 1663<ref name="nk5"/>.
== Rituals ==
Rituals comparable to those held at {{ill|betsugu|ja|別宮|lt=Betsugū|1=Setsumatsusha|2=ja|3=摂末社|4=zh|5=攝末社|6=es|7=Setsumatsusha|8=fr|9=Setsumatsusha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/betsugu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} are performed<ref name="ic"/>. Special ceremonies like the {{ill|Yuki no Ōmike no Gi|ja|由貴大御饌の儀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yuki no Ōmike no Gi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} take place during the {{ill|Sansetsusai|ja|三節祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sansetsusai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} festivals<ref name="gk"/>.
== Cherry Blossoms of Asakuma Shrine ==
Asakuma Shrine is renowned for its cherry blossoms. The poet {{ill|Saigyō|en|Saigyō|qid=Q224689|lt=Saigyō}} composed the following tanka in the {{ill|Shokukokin Wakashū|en|Shokukokin Wakashū|qid=Q1143045|lt=Shokukokin Wakashū}}<ref name="sk92">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p. 192</ref>:
{{Cquote|Calmly I entrust my heart<br> To the divine winds,<br> As the cherry blossoms bloom<br> In the shrine of Sakura.|qq=}}
== Access ==
* Approximately 15 minutes by car from {{ill|Ise interchange|ja|伊勢インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10884857}}.
* Accessible by bus from {{ill|Iseshi Station|en|Iseshi Station|qid=Q6079748|lt=Iseshi Station}} to Asakuma Town.
